page.layout: One printed page, single text column; no marginal notes on the left; a short line of signatures ("§ §") below the text. Running head at top centre above the text.

main_text.p: doctis,atque reipsa,non nomine tenus studiosis,et praeceptoribus meis cum primis gratis et acceptis: quibus cum de studiis aliisque rebus iucunde vtiliterque colloquor.

XX. Professores quoque non raro accedo: atque inde verum esse experior illud, quod quadam in epistola Seneca scribit: nullam rem magis honesta inducere dubios; et in prauum inclinatos ad rectum revocare, quam bonorum virorum cōuersationem: frequenter audiri atque aspici paulatim in pectora descendere praeceptiq; vim obtinere: esse deniq; aliquid, quod ex magno viro, vel tacente, quis discat.
XXI. Familiaritati et amicitiae quorundam ego renunciaui, propterea quod ἰαππῶν pater scripserat, vt eos mufos facerem: ne mea haec in re tergiuersatio aliquam ei suspicionem moueret.
XXII. Tandem non statim a coena, sed vnius ad minimum horae spatio interposito, et recreatiuncu-lis adhibitis honestis, in cubiculum me cum confero, antequam quieti me ac somno dedam, memor illius:
main_text.l: Non prius in dulcem declinat lumina somnum
Omnia quàm longi reputauerit acta diei.
main_text.p: quid eo die audierim, legerim, viderim cogito.
XXIII. Et vt boni patresfamilias accepti atq; expensi habere tabulas solent: ita ephemerides ego et volumina habeo, in quae obseruatu digna refero.
XXIIII. Tandem sacrorum bibliorum lectione piisq; ad Deum votis diem claudo.

page.notes: Signature "§ §" at foot is a printed gathering-style mark, not a catchword. Greek word "ἰαππῶν" in XXI is printed as "Ἰαππῶν"-like form ("διαπ..."); transcribed as printed as far as legible; uncertain letters marked. Page-edge shadow and binding are not transcribed. Several words in the first lines are heavily broken by the scan and were read from context: "doctis" (?), "studiis" (?), "rebus" (?). The Greek word in XXI is doubtful: "ἰαππῶν"[?]. Words "mufos" and "obseruatu" follow the print as far as visible.
